scenes.say: Should you use batch or streaming for your next data pipeline? Let’s break down the trade-offs.

scenes.label: Throughput
scenes.sub: Processes large volumes at intervals, simpler consistency.
scenes.say: Batch processing handles big data sets at scheduled intervals. It’s efficient and easier to keep data consistent.

scenes.label: Latency
scenes.sub: Real-time data, lower latency, but higher complexity.
scenes.say: Streaming processes data as it arrives. You get low latency, but the setup and maintenance are more complex.
For example, batch works well for nightly ETL jobs. Streaming is ideal for real-time fraud detection or live metrics.

scenes.question: Is streaming always better for speed?
scenes.right: Streaming is faster, but adds complexity and overhead. Choose it only if low latency truly matters.
scenes.say: Don’t assume streaming is always better. It’s faster, but the complexity and operational overhead can outweigh the benefits unless low latency is critical.
